record.title: Laborde's path partition conjecture for digraphs
record.statement:
Let $D$ be a digraph, and let $\ell(D)$ denote the order of a longest directed path in $D$. For positive integers $\ell_1$ and $\ell_2$ satisfying

$$
\ell(D)=\ell_1+\ell_2,
$$

a partition of $D$ into two subdigraphs $D_1$ and $D_2$ is a partition whose parts contain all vertices of $D$ and whose longest directed paths have the indicated bounds. **Laborde's path partition conjecture.** For every digraph $D$ and any pair of positive integers $\ell_1$ and $\ell_2$ with $\ell(D)=\ell_1+\ell_2$, there exists a partition of $D$ into two subdigraphs $D_1$ and $D_2$ such that $\ell(D_i)\leq\ell_i$ for $i\in[2]$. This conjecture extends the Gallai–Roy–Vitaver theorem and is known for several generalizations of tournaments, but is open for general digraphs.
record.source_name: Yuefang Sun, “Compositions of Digraphs: A Survey”, arXiv:2103.11171 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.11171

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2021).

record.title: Bondy's strengthened path partition conjecture for digraphs
record.statement:
Let $D$ be a digraph, and let $\ell(D)$ denote the order of a longest directed path in $D$. For positive integers $\ell_1$ and $\ell_2$ satisfying

$$
\ell(D)=\ell_1+\ell_2,
$$

a partition of $D$ into two subdigraphs $D_1$ and $D_2$ is a partition whose parts contain all vertices of $D$. **Bondy's strengthened path partition conjecture.** For every digraph $D$ and any pair of positive integers $\ell_1$ and $\ell_2$ with $\ell(D)=\ell_1+\ell_2$, there exists a partition of $D$ into two subdigraphs $D_1$ and $D_2$ such that $\ell(D_i)=\ell_i$ for $i\in[2]$. This is stated as a stronger version of Laborde's path partition conjecture; the supplied text gives no resolution of the general claim.
record.source_name: Yuefang Sun, “Compositions of Digraphs: A Survey”, arXiv:2103.11171 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.11171

record.title: Arroyo–Galeana-Sánchez's equivalent path partition conjecture
record.statement: Let $D$ be a digraph, and let $\ell(D)$ denote the order of a longest directed path in $D$. For a positive integer $q<\ell(D)$, a partition $(A,B)$ of $V(D)$ determines the induced subdigraphs $D[A]$ and $D[B]$. **Arroyo–Galeana-Sánchez's equivalent path partition conjecture.** For every digraph $D$ and a positive integer $q<\ell(D)$, there exists a partition $(A,B)$ of $V(D)$ such that $\ell(D[A])\leq q$ and $\ell(D[B])\leq\ell(D)-q$. The source states that this formulation is equivalent to Laborde's path partition conjecture and notes that the conjecture has been proved for several classes of digraphs, while leaving the general case unresolved.
record.source_name: Yuefang Sun, “Compositions of Digraphs: A Survey”, arXiv:2103.11171 (2023).

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2021).

record.title: Higher-dimensional Stanley–Wilf conjecture
record.statement:
For $t\geq 2$, let $P$ be a $t$-pattern, and let $T_t(n,P)$ denote the set of all $t$-dimensional $n\times\cdots\times n$ $0$–$1$ matrices avoiding $P$. **Higher-dimensional Stanley–Wilf conjecture.** For every $t$-pattern $P$, there exists a constant $c=c_P$ such that

$$
|T_t(n,P)|\leq c^{n^{t-1}}.
$$

In the source statement, the final display writes $|T_2(n,P)|$, although the surrounding definition and the proposed higher-dimensional generalization use $T_t(n,P)$; the row follows that intended generalization. The conjecture extends the singly exponential bound in dimension two to growth exponential in the number of $(t-1)$-dimensional slices.
record.source_name: Y. Jang, J. Nesetril and P. Ossona de Mendez, “Füredi-Hajnal and Stanley-Wilf conjectures in higher dimensions”, arXiv:2103.14687 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.14687

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2021).

record.title: The extremal-free-word conjecture for avoidable patterns
record.statement:
Let $P$ be an **avoidable pattern**, meaning that arbitrarily long words avoiding $P$ exist over some finite alphabet, and let $\mu(P)$ be the least size of such an alphabet. An extremal $P$-free word is a $P$-free word for which every single-letter extension contains an occurrence of $P$.

**Extremal-free-word conjecture for avoidable patterns.** For every avoidable pattern $P$, there are no extremal $P$-free words over an alphabet of size $\mu(P)+1$.

This generalizes the four-letter square-free extension question to arbitrary avoidable patterns. The paper presents it as an experimental direction and gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Jarosław Grytczuk, Hubert Kordulewski and Bartłomiej Pawlik, “Square-free extensions of words”, arXiv:2104.04841 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.04841

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of April 2021).

record.title: Conjecture on chi-boundedness of graphs excluding induced k-fans
record.statement: For a positive integer $k$, a **$k$-fan** is a graph consisting of an induced path and one additional vertex with at least $k$ neighbours on the path; a $3$-fan is called a **fan**. **The k-fan conjecture.** For every positive integer $k$, the class of graphs with no induced $k$-fan is $\chi$-bounded. This is known for $k\leq 3$, whereas the assertion for general $k$ remains open; it strengthens the Aboulker–Bousquet conjecture because a $k$-fan contains an induced cycle with exactly $k-2$ chords.
record.source_name: James Davies, “Triangle-free graphs with large chromatic number and no induced wheel”, arXiv:2104.05907 (2022).

record.title: The finite-group extension conjecture for group-labeled graph lifts
record.statement:
Let $n\ge 3$ be an integer and let $\Gamma$ be a finite group. Let $K_n^{\Gamma}$ be the fully $\Gamma$-labeled complete graph, and let $\mathcal{M}_{n,\Gamma}$ denote the class of matroids considered in the paper. Write $M(K_n^{\Gamma})$ for the cycle matroid of the underlying graph. **The finite-group extension conjecture.** If $M\in\mathcal{M}_{n,\Gamma}$ and

$$
r(M)-r(M(K_n^{\Gamma}))>1,
$$

then there is a prime $p$ and an integer $j\ge 2$ such that

$$
\Gamma\cong \mathbb{Z}_p^j.
$$

The abelian-group version is proved in the paper, and the conjecture proposes the same conclusion for all finite groups. Its status remains open.
record.source_name: Zach Walsh, “A new matroid lift construction and an application to group-labeled graphs”, arXiv:2104.08257 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.08257

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2021).

record.title: The integer-move conjecture for the fractional transversal game
record.statement: Let $H=(V,\mathcal E)$ be a finite hypergraph. An **integer move** in the fractional transversal game is a move of the form $(v_{i_1},1)$. **Integer-move conjecture.** If each of the first $2k-1$ moves, for $k\geq 1$, was an integer move, then Staller has an integer move in the $(2k)^{\rm th}$ turn that is optimal in the fractional transversal game. This would mean that fractional moves are advantageous only for Edge-hitter. The conjecture is presented as open and would imply the weaker inequality $\tau_g^*(H)\leq\tau_g(H)$ for every hypergraph.
record.source_name: Csilla Bujtás, Günter Rote and Zsolt Tuza, “Optimal strategies in fractional games: vertex cover and domination”, arXiv:2105.03890 (2021).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.03890

record.title: Partition sumset Bohr-set conjecture for finite-index endomorphisms
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a (not necessarily countable) abelian group, let $d\geq 3$, and let $\phi_1,\dots,\phi_d$ be endomorphisms of $G$ such that $[G:\phi_j(G)]<\infty$ for each $j$. Suppose that $S\subset [d]$ is non-empty and

$$
\sum_{j\in S}\phi_j=0.
$$

**Partition sumset Bohr-set conjecture.** For every finite partition $G=\bigcup_{i=1}^r A_i$, there exists $i\in [r]$ such that

$$
\sum_{j=1}^d\phi_j(A_i)
$$

contains a Bohr-$(k,\eta)$ set, where $k$ and $\eta$ depend only on $r$ and the indices $[G:\phi_j(G)]$. This extends the corresponding partition result and remains conjectural in the stated generality.
record.source_name: John T. Griesmer, Anh N. Le and Thái Hoàng Lê, “Bohr sets in sumsets II: countable abelian groups”, arXiv:2207.04150 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.04150

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2022).

record.title: Pseudoperiodic word avoidance conjecture for binary words
record.statement: Let $(a,b)$ be a pair of positive integers with $1\leq a<b$. An infinite binary word has **pseudoperiod** $(a,b)$ if each position is compatible with a repetition having periods $a$ and $b$; a word is **avoiding $3^+$-powers** if it contains no factor whose exponent is at least $3$. **Pseudoperiodic word avoidance conjecture.** For all pairs $(a,b)$ with $1\leq a<b$ and $b\ne 2a$, there exists an infinite binary word with pseudoperiod $(a,b)$ and avoiding $3^+$-powers. The conjecture is motivated by the observed critical exponents in the computed examples, all of which are at most $3^+$; its general case remains open.
record.source_name: Joseph Meleshko, Pascal Ochem, Jeffrey Shallit and Sonja Linghui Shan, “Pseudoperiodic Words and a Question of Shevelev”, arXiv:2207.10171 (2023).

record.title: Ferdinand's girth conjecture for the bipartite graph D(k,q)
record.statement: Let $D(k,q)$ be the bipartite graph originally proposed by Lazebnik and Ustimenko, where $k$ is an integer not less than $2$ and $q$ is a prime power. The graph has girth at least $k+4$ for $k\geq 3$. **Ferdinand's girth conjecture.** $D(k,q)$ has girth $k+5$ for all odd $k$ and all $q\geq 4$. This conjecture concerns the exact girth of the highly symmetric graphs $D(k,q)$, which are also used in extremal graph theory, finite geometry, coding theory and related applications. Its resolution status is not established by the supplied text.
record.source_name: Ming Xu, Xiaoyan Cheng and Yuansheng Tang, “On the girth cycles of the bipartite graph D(k,q)”, arXiv:2207.12752 (2022).

record.title: List steady-word conjecture for four-letter alphabets
record.statement:
A word $W=w_1w_2\cdots w_n$ is **steady** if it is square-free and remains square-free after deleting any single letter. Let $n$ be a positive integer, and let $\mathcal{A}_1,\mathcal{A}_2,\ldots,\mathcal{A}_n$ be alphabets, each of size $4$.

**List steady-word conjecture.** There exists a steady word $W=w_1w_2\cdots w_n$ such that $w_i\in\mathcal{A}_i$ for every $i=1,2,\ldots,n$.

The paper proves the corresponding statement for alphabets of size at least $7$. The analogous conjecture for pure square-free words is discussed separately and is not this claim; no resolution of the four-letter steady-word version is supplied here.
record.source_name: Michał Dębski, Jarosław Grytczuk and Bartłomiej Pawlik, “Extensions and reductions of square-free words”, arXiv:2209.08507 (2022).

record.title: The conjecture for extensions beginning with n1 and n2
record.statement:
Let $L(w)$ denote the lexicographically least infinite word on $\mathbb{N}$ beginning with $w$ whose only square factors are contained in the prefix $w$. **The conjecture for extensions beginning with $n1$ and $n2$.** For every integer $n\geq 3$,

$$
L(n1)=nL(1)\qquad\text{and}\qquad L(n2)=nL(2).
$$

These identities would extend the known formulas for prefixes $nn$ and $n_1n_2$ with letters at least $3$, and would describe the least square-free extensions of the mixed prefixes $n1$ and $n2$.

record.title: The fixed-size MSTD–MDTS conjecture for dihedral groups
record.statement:
Let $D_{2n}$ be the dihedral group of order $2n$. For a positive integer $m$, let $\mathcal S_{2n,m}$ denote the collection of subsets of $D_{2n}$ of size $m$. A subset is **MSTD** if its sumset has greater cardinality than its difference set, and **MDTS** if its difference set has greater cardinality than its sumset.

**Fixed-size MSTD–MDTS conjecture.** For every integer $n\geq 3$ and every $m\leq 2n$, the collection $\mathcal S_{2n,m}$ has at least as many MSTD sets as MDTS sets.

The source reports that this conjecture is known for $m=2$, $m=3$, and $m>n$; the general fixed-size assertion remains open in the supplied text.

record.title: The St. Ives matching conjecture for online path Ramsey numbers
record.statement:
For each $k\geq 1$, let $S_k$ be the St. Ives ordered matching defined recursively from two disjoint consecutive copies of $S_{k-1}$ by adding an edge whose endpoints lie respectively to the left and right of both copies. Let $r_o(S_k,P_n)$ denote the online Ramsey number for finding an ordered copy of $S_k$ or an ordered path $P_n$.

**St. Ives matching conjecture.** For all $k\geq 1$, there is a constant $c_k$ such that for all $n\geq 1$,

$$
r_o(S_k,P_n)\leq n+c_k.
$$

Every intersection-free matching on $k$ edges is a subgraph of $S_k$, so this statement is equivalent to the intersection-free matching conjecture. The source gives no resolution of the conjecture.
record.source_name: Felix Christian Clemen, Emily Heath and Mikhail Lavrov, “Online Ramsey numbers of ordered paths and cycles”, arXiv:2210.05235 (2024).
record.references:

record.title: Conjectured relation between permutations generating two and three CNATs
record.statement: Let $b(n,k)$ be the number of distinct permutations of $n$ letters that give rise to exactly $k$ CNATs. **CNAT-count relation conjecture.** For all $k\geq 1$, $b(n,2)=b(n+1,3)$. The statement is presented as a conjecture based on further numerical experimentation; no proof or resolution is given. The quantifier over $k$ appears inconsistent with the displayed equation, which does not depend on $k$.
record.source_name: Daniel Chen and Sebastian Ohlig, “Associated Permutations of Complete Non-Ambiguous Trees”, arXiv:2210.11117 (2024).

record.title: Conjecture that every nontrivial tree is harmonious
record.statement: A graph $G$ is **harmonious** when it admits a harmonious labeling, namely an injective vertex labeling whose induced edge labels are also injective modulo $|E(G)|$; for trees, the definition allows at most one repeated vertex label. A tree is **nontrivial** if it has at least one edge. **Harmonious-tree conjecture.** Every nontrivial tree is harmonious. Many classes of trees are known to be harmonious, and super edge-magic trees are known to be harmonious, but the assertion for all trees remains open.
record.source_name: Rikio Ichishima, S. C. López, Francesc A. Muntaner-Batle and Yukio Takahashi, “Recent studies on the super edge-magic deficiency of graphs”, arXiv:2211.04029 (2022).

record.title: The e-positivity conjecture for chromatic quasisymmetric functions of indifference graphs
record.statement:
Let $\gamma$ be an indifference graph, and write its chromatic quasisymmetric function in the elementary symmetric-function basis as

$$
X_{\gamma}(\mathbf{x};t)=\sum_{\lambda}a_{\lambda}(t)e_{\lambda}.
$$

**The e-positivity conjecture.** For each $\gamma \in \mathcal{I}\mathcal{G}$, $X_{\gamma}(\mathbf{x};t)$ is $e$-positive; equivalently, $a_{\lambda}(t)\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}[t]$ for every partition $\lambda$.

This conjecture generalizes the Stanley–Stembridge conjecture, whose $t=1$ case is known. The full polynomial positivity statement remains open.
record.source_name: Lucas Gagnon, “A unipotent realization of the chromatic quasisymmetric function”, arXiv:2211.06981 (2023).

record.title: Cichacz–Suchan irregular-labeling conjecture for digraphs
record.statement:
Let $\overrightarrow{G}$ be a digraph of order $n$ whose weakly connected components all have order at least $3$, and let $\Gamma$ be an Abelian group. A **$\Gamma$-irregular labeling** is a labeling in which the vertex weights are distinct, as defined in the surrounding discussion. **Cichacz–Suchan's irregular-labeling conjecture.** There exists a constant $K$ such that every such digraph $\overrightarrow{G}$ has a $\Gamma$-irregular labeling for every Abelian group $\Gamma$ satisfying

$$
|\Gamma|\geq n+K.
$$

This is presented as a conjecture based on bounds previously obtained for components of order at least $4$ and for groups of size greater than $(1+\varepsilon)n$; no resolution is given.
record.source_name: Sylwia Cichacz, “Disjoint zero-sum subsets in Abelian groups and its application – survey”, arXiv:2410.22245 (2024).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2022–2024). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2203.09395](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.09395).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.22245

record.title: Positive matching decomposition conjecture for Cartesian products of cycles
record.statement:
Let $C_m$ and $C_n$ be cycles with $m,n\geq3$, and let $\mathrm{pmd}(G)$ denote the positive matching decomposition number. **Positive matching decomposition conjecture for Cartesian products of cycles.**

$$
\mathrm{pmd}(C_m\square C_n)=6
$$

for all $m,n\geq3$ such that $m+n$ is even, or such that $(m,n)\in\{(3,4),(3,6),(5,6)\}$. The supplied text presents this exact-value assertion after an analysis of positive matchings in the relevant Cartesian products; no resolution beyond that analysis is provided.
record.source_name: Mohammad Farrokhi Derakhshandeh Ghouchan and Ali Akbar Yazdan Pour, “Positive matching decompositions of the cartesian product of graphs”, arXiv:2502.02826 (2025).
record.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2022–2025). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2405.20480](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.20480), [arXiv:2202.10463](https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.10463).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.02826
